slides.title: Default Arguments and Overloading Rules
slides.prompt: Default parameters specify fallback values if arguments are omitted. Function overloading allows multiple functions with the same name but distinct parameter signatures.

slides.title: Default Parameter Assignment
slides.prompt: Fill in the default value syntax in parameter declaration.

slides.title: Default Arguments Trailing Rule
slides.prompt: Where must default arguments be placed in a function parameter list?
options: At the end of the parameter list (trailing parameters)
At the beginning of the parameter list
In the middle between required parameters
slides.correctAnswer: At the end of the parameter list (trailing parameters)

slides.title: Declaration Placement for Defaults
slides.prompt: Default values should be declared in prototype headers, NOT repeated in definitions. Fill in parameter name.

slides.title: Overload Resolution Criteria
slides.prompt: Which criteria determine a valid function overload signature in C++?
options: Number, types, and sequence of parameters (Return type alone is NOT sufficient)
slides.correctAnswer: Number, types, and sequence of parameters (Return type alone is NOT sufficient)

slides.title: Ambiguous Call Hazard
slides.prompt: Combining default parameters with overloading can cause ambiguous calls. Identify parameter count for error.

slides.title: Name Mangling Mechanism
slides.prompt: How does the C++ compiler support function overloading under the hood?
options: Name Mangling (decorating symbol names with parameter type information)
slides.correctAnswer: Name Mangling (decorating symbol names with parameter type information)

slides.title: Disabling Name Mangling
slides.prompt: Fill in linkage specification to export function with standard C linkage.

slides.title: Const Overloading on Reference Types
slides.prompt: Can functions be overloaded based on 'const T&' versus 'T&' parameter qualification?
options: Yes, the compiler resolves rvalues/const lvalues to const T& and mutable lvalues to T&
No, const qualifications are ignored during overload resolution
Only if return types differ as well
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, the compiler resolves rvalues/const lvalues to const T& and mutable lvalues to T&
